hints: Notice the two given forces on the object: one horizontal to the right and one longer force to the north-east.
Recall that to add vectors you place them tip-to-tail, keeping their directions unchanged, and the resultant runs from the first tail to the second tip.
Check which labelled $F$ starts where the horizontal force starts and ends where the north-east force ends, pointing north-east between them.
walkthrough: Identify the given vectors: a short horizontal force to the east and a longer force to the north-east, both starting at the object.
State the triangle rule: place the tail of the second vector at the tip of the first vector without rotating either vector.
The resultant $F$ is the single vector that completes the triangle, drawn from the tail of the first-placed force to the tip of the second-placed force.
In the correct diagram the horizontal arrow is drawn first, the north-east arrow starts at its tip, and $F$ joins the left-most tail to the right-most tip pointing north-east.
Only diagram D shows this tip-to-tail arrangement with $F$ as the closing side in the forward direction. This is option D.

A.explanation: The arrow labelled $F$ is drawn as one side of the triangle, not from the start of the first force to the end of the second force.

B.explanation: The arrow labelled $F$ is drawn as one side of the triangle and points roughly north, not in the north-east direction of the combined pull.

C.explanation: The arrow labelled $F$ points to the south-west, opposite to the direction obtained by adding a eastward and a north-eastward force.

D.explanation: The two forces are placed tip-to-tail and $F$ joins the tail of the first to the tip of the second, giving the correct north-east resultant.
